reason: The filesystem contract is kept as a Go contract package: one interface, typed service keys, the error table and three typed events. Each operation takes the unresolved path and the per-call policy.
The local-disk provider is kept: identity, atomic publication, per-target serialisation and guards. It is rebuilt on the fsx helpers and rooted handles, and its version token gains a content digest.

The fence is no longer a subclass that replaces the provider. Enforcing the per-call policy is part of every provider's contract, and the local provider does it with os.Root handles on the write roots.

The pure patch parser and text applier become the sub-package textdiff/patch of the shared textdiff package, ported rule for rule from the pinned Codex behaviour, with line-ending handling moved inside.

Read-before-edit stays an optional listener with no service of its own. Its state becomes a projection over logged observation events instead of an in-memory map, and it ships disabled as upstream does.
The read, write, edit, apply_patch and read_image tools keep their names, arguments, result envelopes and guidance. They become thin front ends over one operation service.
The glob and grep tools are kept, but the child rg process is replaced by the in-process search package reading through the filesystem provider, and the pattern dialect becomes Go RE2.
The single-editor tool is kept as an optional, default-off tool with the same commands and schema, implemented as a front end over the operation service so it cannot skip the fence or the policy.
The fixed guidance paragraph becomes a prompt section of the deliver/present component, rendered only for a carrier that declares it shows file links.
The present tool and its log-only event are kept. A declaration additionally records a digest and keeps a bounded copy in the blob store.

The per-turn changed-files recorder is kept with its Git snapshots and file-tool captures. The summary moves into the event and the hunks into the blob store, and a manifest covers directories without Git.

The guidance section is rendered only when the carrier declares that it shows file links, and its card sentences only when it shows cards and present is visible, so the text never promises a rendering the host lacks.
No desktop application opens the file. The host opens it once and checks and streams from that one handle, so there is no gap between the check and the open.
A declaration stores a digest and a bounded copy. The card says when the source changed or is missing and can open the copy, within the stated size bound.
The delivered copy is a blob referenced by the event, which is the persistent delivery version upstream deferred. Whether an export bundles blobs is the export owner's decision.
The workspace/changes event carries the whole summary and references a blob holding the hunks, so cards and comparisons are served from the log after a host restart.

Git is run with core.splitIndex and the LFS filters switched off for the call. A real-Git scenario checks that the user's Git directory is unchanged, and a repository class where it is not uses the manifest instead.
A Git failure no longer abandons the turn. The recorder falls back to manifest and captures and records the coverage used and the reason in the event.
Temporary space is bounded: untracked files above maxFileBytes are excluded from the snapshot, and above snapshotMaxBytes in total the turn uses the manifest.

Each listed file is labelled tool, when a file tool changed it, or other, when it changed during the turn by something else, and the card shows the label. The summary no longer claims the turn made a change it cannot attribute.
Without a repository a manifest of the working directory is taken at turn start and end, so shell edits are listed as added, modified or deleted. A comparison exists where a before side exists.
Ignored files and files outside the working directory are still listed only when a file tool names them. The event's coverage field says so and the card shows it.
justification: Walking ignored trees every turn costs more than it tells, and files outside the write roots cannot be enumerated. The limit is stated in the event and shown on the card; DH-D-FS-9 builds it.

reason: The recorder evaluates ignore rules in process and skips the capture for a path the turn's snapshot already covers, so a covered file is not copied a second time.
Only bounded hunks are stored and rendered, never a file's complete text. A compareScope setting lists files outside the workspace without content, and the route declares the resources it reads.
A coarse comparison above hunkMaxBytes carries line counts only, so a degraded result no longer holds every line of both sides.
Stored paths use forward slashes on every platform and are converted to the host form only at the boundary.
There is no unfenced provider to mount. The base directory is only a default for relative paths, and containment comes from the per-call policy enforced by the provider.
Watch delegates to the one harness watch service, whose requirements and tests cover a parent directory that is deleted and recreated.
A version carries a SHA-256 of the content wherever the content was read, and the digest decides, so a storage layer that does not update metadata no longer defeats the stale check.
Memory is bounded by a constant instead of by file size: a text mutation refuses a file above textMaxBytes with fs/too-large.
A mutation outcome carries hunks computed under the provider's lock within the diff size bounds. No whole before or after text is returned or retained.
One text classifier in fsx is applied to the whole content on the read path and the edit path, so a file with a late NUL byte gets the same verdict from both.
Harness processes serialise on a cross-process lock keyed by file identity. Programs that take no lock are detected by a version re-check immediately before publication, with or without a guard.
Where the filesystem refuses hard links, create-if-absent reserves the name with an exclusive create and renames the staged file over the reservation.

Staging is one file beside the target that the publishing rename consumes, so there is no staging directory to remove afterwards. A file left by a failure has a recognisable prefix and is swept by age.
Observations are log-only session events folded by a registered projection, so a resumed session has them, and the digest check makes an observation of a since-changed file stale.
The operation service refuses a file tool call that carries no session before it runs, so there is no caller that may run the tool yet can never satisfy the policy.
Observation is recorded by the operation service, not by one tool, so every tool that shows file content to the model through it counts as having read the file.
An observation records whether the whole file or a part was shown, and the setting overwriteRequires: full-view demands the stronger rule. The default stays freshness by a recorded decision.
The patch applier detects, normalises, matches and restores the line-ending style itself, so no caller owns the conversion.
The parser is a line-fed state machine that reports each finished operation as input arrives. Applying works on complete text that textMaxBytes already bounds.

Mutations under workspace-write go through os.Root handles, which refuse a name that resolves outside the root, closing the check-to-write race. Mount points inside a root remain the operator's responsibility.
The fence takes its write roots only from the policy value issued by the one resolver, and a test fails if a filesystem package computes roots itself.
The provider requires the policy resolver as an injected service and does not load without it, so a composition cannot end up with file tools and no fence.
A move without hunks becomes a byte-preserving rename that accepts any regular file. Edits and patches still require UTF-8 text.
justification: Editing by literal match needs one known encoding, so text tools stay UTF-8 only by decision DH-ADR-FS-11. DH-D-FS-4 builds the narrowed rule.

reason: A plain move inside one write root that may replace its destination is one atomic rename. A move that must not replace, applies hunks or crosses roots is still two effects.
justification: os.Root offers no rename that refuses to replace, so creating one name and removing another cannot be one step. The outcome states both effects; DH-D-FS-4 builds it.

reason: Every operation takes a do-not-follow-the-final-link option, removing the separate lstat step. Copy and recursive directory operations stay outside the provider contract.
justification: No model-facing tool needs copy or recursive operations; the shell covers them under the process sandbox. Kept by decision DH-ADR-FS-11 and built by DH-D-FS-4.

reason: Every operation takes a context.Context and the operation service applies a default deadline that acts at check points up to the start of publication.
Each operation takes the unresolved path and returns the resolved target in its outcome, so a remote provider needs one round trip per tool call.
Search walks the filesystem provider's own view from the session's working directory and returns the provider's display paths, so a returned path is readable by the read tool by construction.
There is no bundled binary: search is code inside the one harness binary, and a remote provider is searched through its view or runs the same package on its side.
The walk starts at the literal prefix of the pattern and does not enter a directory under which no match can lie.
Both tools take an offset, grep takes an output mode (lines, files or count), and the description teaches (?i) for case. Paging through a complete result no longer needs a spill store.
Over-cap sampling splits its budget across the children of each directory level in turn, not only across top-level entries.
A patch commit is still not rolled back; the report lists every operation as completed, failed, unknown or not executed.
justification: Undoing earlier operations could overwrite an outside edit made meanwhile, which is upstream's recorded reason. Kept by decision DH-ADR-FS-11; DH-D-FS-6 builds the report.

reason: The read tool returns a bounded one-level listing for a directory instead of refusing it, which gives the model a directory listing without another tool.
The directory error is gone and a non-text file is answered with the tool that reads it. The read tool still reads UTF-8 text only; audio and video are not read.
justification: read stays a text tool: images go to read_image and documents to the document area. Kept by decision DH-ADR-FS-11; DH-D-FS-6 builds the routing hint.

reason: The file signature decides the image type and the extension is not consulted, so a valid image under a wrong extension is accepted.
read_image asks the attachment store whether the path is one of its objects and returns the existing reference, so a stored image is not admitted a second time against the source limits.

The limit exists only because upstream's React client fills a plugin slot to show the image. The Go UI has no client plugin slots; the tool's own server-rendered card shows the image from the reference in the result.
read_image accepts an attachment reference as well as a path and an optional region, so a pasted image without a path can be re-read in part.
File tools run under a context deadline applied by the operation service, so a call has a time budget even though one system call cannot be interrupted.
The single-editor tool still handles UTF-8 text only, as every text tool in this area does.
justification: Editing by literal match needs one known encoding; text tools stay UTF-8 only by decision DH-ADR-FS-11. DH-D-FS-8 builds the tool.

reason: str_replace still requires exactly one match and has no replace_all argument.
justification: The tool exists for the schema some models already know, so it is not extended; the edit tool offers replace_all. Kept by decision DH-ADR-FS-11; DH-D-FS-8 builds it.

reason: The tool is a front end over the operation service, which always applies the fence and asks for an intent decision, so no composition gives it unconditional mutations.

The Go harness exposes glob with the same name and arguments plus an optional offset. It runs in process, walks only where the pattern can match, and still includes hidden and ignored files but not version-control directories.

The Go harness exposes grep with the same name and arguments plus optional output and offset. The pattern dialect changes from ripgrep syntax to Go RE2, which the description and the invalid-pattern error state.
The Go harness exposes apply_patch with the input argument, whole-patch preflight and ordered commit without rollback. It is on by default, following the upstream defaults note.
The Go harness exposes edit with the same arguments and result sentence. It is always fenced, bounded in size and re-checks the file before publishing.
The Go harness exposes read with the same arguments, envelope, footers and limits. A directory is listed instead of refused, and a non-text file is answered with the tool that reads it.
The Go harness exposes read_image while an attachment store is mounted. The file signature decides the type, and the tool also accepts an attachment reference and an optional region.
The Go harness exposes write with the same arguments and result envelope. It is always fenced, and content above the text size bound is refused.
The Go harness exposes present with the same arguments and result lines. A declaration also records a digest and keeps a bounded copy.
The Go harness can expose str_replace_editor with the same commands and schema. It is off unless a preset enables it.
Folded into the one around event fs.Intent, whose request names the operation (delete) and whose result is a closed decision where the strictest answer wins.
Folded into the one around event fs.Intent, whose request names the operation (edit, patch or move-source) and whose result is a closed decision where the strictest answer wins.
Folded into the one around event fs.Intent, whose request names the operation (write or move-destination) and whose result is a closed decision where the strictest answer wins.
Kept as the notify event fs.Observed, which contains listener failures, and additionally written as a log-only durable fs/observed session event so that observations survive a restart.
Replaced by the Go struct local.Config (baseDir, textMaxBytes); the diff basis bound moves to ops.Config as size limits for the diff package.
The fence has no configuration of its own in Go. It is part of the local provider, and its mode and write roots come from the policy resolver for each call.
Replaced by the Go struct tools.Config with the same switches and read limits. applyPatch defaults to true, and readStreamMinSize is gone because every read streams.
Replaced by the Go struct tools.SearchConfig with the result caps and timeout. The three fields that described the child process are gone, and sampleOverCap gets the default every shipped row states.
Replaced by the Go struct present.Config: maxFiles as upstream, plus keepCopy and copyMaxBytes for the delivered copy.
Replaced by the Go struct tools.EditorConfig: an enabled switch that defaults to false, maxOutputChars and the description.
Replaced by the Go struct changes.Config: the Git limits and file caps as upstream, new budgets for snapshot, manifest and turn diff, and no diff time limit because the diff bound is input size.
ctx.fs becomes the service key fs.Key holding the fs.FileSystem interface, a direct seam. Model-facing tools use a second key, fs.OpsKey, for the operation service.
ctx.workspaceChanges becomes the service key deliver.ChangesKey holding the deliver.Changes interface (Summary and Diff), answered from the session log and the blob store instead of host memory.

title: The decision note and two READMEs say apply_patch ships enabled, but the shipped base row and Web standard preset say applyPatch: false

reason: A default is a Go value and the configuration catalog is generated from the running registry, so a document cannot state a default the product does not have. The Go default follows the note.

title: The search README says both tools include hidden and ignored files, but grep passes neither --hidden nor --no-ignore

reason: Each tool's description states its own rule for hidden and ignored files, and a golden test pins the description and the behaviour together.

title: The intent, provider and observation steps are written out separately in three tool implementations, so a tool that omits them is unguarded

reason: One operation service performs path resolution, policy, intent, the provider call and the observation for every file tool; a tool holds only its schema and its result text.

title: Intent waterfalls have one first-wins slot by registration order, and a throwing fs/observed listener fails a tool call whose write already succeeded

reason: The intent event returns a closed decision where the strictest answer wins whatever the registration order, and observation is a notify event whose listener failures are contained.

The read guidance sentence is carried word for word and pinned by a golden test. The note rests on an observed session that read line ranges with sed 60 times; its own benchmark measured the sentence as neutral.

Declaring files without copying is kept as the base, but the note's deferral of stored copies no longer holds: the Go design has a blob store and no desktop application, so a declaration also records a digest and keeps a bounded copy.

The patch format, the input argument name, whole-patch preflight, ordered commit without rollback and the stated outcome of a half-finished move are kept; the parser and matcher are ported from the pinned Codex rules.

The Go defaults follow the note: apply_patch on (decided by the owner, DH-ADR-35) and read-before-edit off. The pinned shipped rows say applyPatch: false, against the note and the READMEs; that contradiction is recorded as UP-DEBT-found.A08.1.
